title: World Peace Cookies (Korova Cookies)
description: Rich chocolate shortbread with bittersweet chunks and flaky sea salt.
instructions:
Make the cookie dough: With a stand mixer fitted with a paddle attachment or with a hand mixer in a large bowl, beat the butter with the brown and granulated sugars, kosher salt, and vanilla until soft and creamy. If you started with cold butter in a stand mixer, you’ll need to beat it for several minutes until it’s smooth, scraping down the bowl two or three times so that it evenly mixes.
Sift the flour, cocoa and baking soda right into the butter mixture. On low speed, carefully (so it doesn’t go flying) mix the flour mixture into the butter mixture just until the flour disappears into the dough, scraping it down as needed. The dough will look a little crumbly. Add the chocolate pieces and mix only to incorporate.
Shape the cookie dough: Turn the dough out onto a large piece of parchment paper (I’m using a 13×18-inch one for a half-sheet pan) and shape it into a log about 2 inches in diameter and 15-16″ long. Roll the log in the parchment paper and chill for 3 hours, until firm. If you’re going to chill it longer such as overnight or for a couple days, wrap the log in plastic wrap too, so it doesn’t dry out.
Bake the cookies: Heat your oven to 325°F (160°C). Line two large baking sheets with parchment paper. Working with a sharp thin knife, slice the logs into rounds that are 1/2-inch thick. (The rounds are likely to crack as you’re cutting them — don’t be concerned, just squeeze the bits back onto each cookie.) Arrange the rounds on the baking sheets, leaving about one inch between them. Sprinkle each cookie with a flake or two of sea salt.
Bake cookies, one sheet a time for even baking, for about 12 minutes. They will be very soft and look completely underbaked, but that’s just the way they should be. Transfer the baking sheet to a cooling rack and let the cookies rest until they are only just warm, at which point you can serve them or transfer them to a cooling rack.
Do ahead: Cookies keep in an airtight container at room temperature for 1 week, or so I’ve heard. (It’s never happened.) You can also freeze them tightly packed in a container for up a month. You can freeze the log of unbaked dough, wrapped in plastic, for up to 2 months. No need to defrost before baking. They usually just need 1 more minute of baking time.
Notes: Here are the changes I made in the recipe between the 2007 and 2025 version:

I rescaled the recipe, increasing it, so I can use a full two “sticks” or 8-ounce package of butter (vs. the 11 tablespoons in the original).
When using a stand mixer, I start with cold butter.
If you’d like to start with salted butter, skip the kosher salt in the dough.
I make one larger log of dough vs. two smaller ones. The final cookies are somewhat larger/heftier, making a single cookie the ideal serving size.

ingredients.note: cold and diced for stand mixer or at room temp for a hand mixer
ingredients.raw: 16 tablespoons (225 grams) unsalted butter, cold and diced for stand mixer or at room temp for a hand mixer
1 cup (215 grams) packed light brown sugar

ingredients.note: or a generous 1 cup storebought mini chocolate chips
ingredients.raw: 8 ounces (225 grams) bittersweet chocolate, chopped into chips, or a generous 1 cup storebought mini chocolate chips

ingredients.item: A few pinches of flaky sea salt
ingredients.raw: A few pinches of flaky sea salt
